landscape.hook: Can you explain redacted, AccessibilityFocusState and UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor in English?

dialogue.title: The last SwiftUI day

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, this is our last SwiftUI day. The list looks broken while the data loads.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use redacted with `.placeholder`. SwiftUI shows gray blocks instead of the real text.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So redacted keeps the layout and hides the text?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, and you remove redacted when the data arrives.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now accessibility. After saving, VoiceOver stays on the old button.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use AccessibilityFocusState. It moves the VoiceOver focus to a view you choose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I set `focus` to true, and VoiceOver jumps to the message?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Mark the message view with the same AccessibilityFocusState.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last, a library needs an app delegate, and SwiftUI has none.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor. It connects your delegate class to the SwiftUI app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where do I put the UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In your App type, as a property. That is a great finish for SwiftUI.
